title: Attorney General of Illinois

context.text: Both primaries (March 17, 2026) were effectively uncontested at the top: Raoul was unopposed for the Democratic nomination; Fioretti won the Republican primary with 99.4% against a write-in candidate.
Raoul has been Attorney General since 2019 and won his last two elections by more than 11 points, according to the Sun-Times and WBEZ.
The State Board of Elections' candidate list for the Nov. 3, 2026 general election shows two active Attorney General candidates, Raoul (Democratic) and Fioretti (Republican).

candidates.name: Kwame Raoul
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the March 17 Democratic primary.

summary.text: Kwame Raoul is the Democratic Attorney General of Illinois, seeking a third term. A former Cook County prosecutor and state senator (2004-2019), he has filed or joined numerous lawsuits against Trump administration actions on funding, tariffs and immigration enforcement.

background.text: Born in Chicago; earned a bachelor's degree from DePaul University (1987) and a law degree from Chicago-Kent College of Law.
Worked as a prosecutor in the Cook County State's Attorney's Office and as a partner at Quarles & Brady LLP.
Served in the Illinois State Senate, District 13, from 2004 to 2019; elected Attorney General in 2018.

priorities.text: Defending Illinois's federal funding and legal interests in court against Trump administration actions.
Consumer protection and antitrust enforcement, including a suit to block the Nexstar-TEGNA merger.

positions.summary: Sued in March 2026 as part of a 22-attorney-general coalition to block the Trump administration's latest tariffs, which he called another round of price increases on Americans.
positions.quote: President Trump is doubling down on his failed economic policies by imposing another round of price increases on Americans.

statements.quote: Border Patrol agents and ICE officers have acted as occupiers rather than officers of the law.
statements.context: On the lawsuit he filed over CBP and ICE tactics in Illinois.

record.text: Sued DHS and Trump administration officials over CBP and ICE tactics in Illinois, with the City of Chicago as a co-plaintiff, alleging violations of the Tenth Amendment and the Administrative Procedure Act.
Sued with the attorneys general of California, Colorado, Minnesota and New York to challenge a federal freeze of $10 billion in child care and family funding.
Joined a 22-attorney-general coalition suit challenging the administration's second round of tariffs under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974.
Joined seven other attorneys general in suing to block Nexstar Media Group's acquisition of TEGNA.

candidates.researchNotes: His campaign site did not load (bot challenge). Issue positions are limited to the statements in his office's releases.

candidates.name: Bob Fioretti
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17 Republican primary with 99.4%.

summary.text: Bob Fioretti is the Republican nominee for Attorney General. A Chicago attorney and former two-term alderman of the 2nd Ward (2007-2015), he has run unsuccessfully for mayor, Cook County state's attorney and Cook County Board president.

background.text: Earned a B.A. in political science from the University of Illinois and a J.D. from Northern Illinois University; practiced as a civil rights attorney.
Served as Chicago alderman for the 2nd Ward from 2007 to 2015 and, according to the Sun-Times, as an assistant Illinois attorney general.

priorities.text: Restore public trust and fight corruption, saying he would lead 'with integrity and independence.'
Crime and public safety, citing his courtroom experience with the Chicago corporation counsel's office.

candidates.researchNotes: His campaign site has no issue pages; priorities are limited to its slogan and the Sun-Times summary. Not an incumbent in this office; no record to list.
